description: SOC-thermal model for aluminum-ion batteries: V = OCV(SOC) - I*R(T)
source: Lin et al. (2015) Nature; Pang et al. (2019) Joule; Guo et al. (2020) Energy Storage Mater.

cell.name: Aluminum-Ion (Al-graphite in AlCl3:EMImCl ionic liquid)
cell.note: Al^3+ insertion into graphite cathode; Al anode dissolution. E ~ 2.0 V vs Al/Al^3+

nominal_voltage.note: Nominal voltage (plateau near 2 V). Lin et al. 2015 Nature

R_ref.note: Internal resistance at T_ref; ionic liquid electrolyte has moderate conductivity

ocv_coefficients.description: OCV(SOC) polynomial for Al-ion battery (two-plateau behavior: ~2.2 V and ~1.8 V)
ocv_coefficients.source: Lin et al. (2015) Nature 520, 324-328; Pang et al. (2019) Joule 3(1), 136-148
ocv_coefficients.note: Two-step intercalation: Stage 1 ~2.2V, Stage 2 ~1.8V. Polynomial captures average. Pang 2019

E_a.note: Activation energy for Al-ion resistance. Ionic liquid shows moderate T-sensitivity. Guo 2020

alpha_c.note: Capacity T-coefficient. Ionic liquid viscosity decreases with T -> better ion transport. Guo 2020

dOCV_dT.note: Entropic coefficient for Al-ion. Slight negative (entropy decreases on Al insertion). Pang 2019

current.note: Al-ion can support high C-rates. Lin 2015

temperature.note: Limited by ionic liquid freezing point
